newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZCC declines to clear Goodman/Defiance deal.
newsitem.headline: NZCC declines to clear Goodman/Defiance deal.

text.p: The New Zealand Commerce Commission on Monday declined to clear Goodman Fielder Ltd to acquire the New Zealand milling and baking assets of Defiance Mills Ltd.

Chairman of the anti-monopolies commission Alan Bollard said the commission was not satisfied that, should the acquisition go ahead, Goodman Fielder would not acquire or strengthen a dominant position in any markets.
Bollard said the commission defined 15 markets relevant to the acquisition and investigated what impact the proposed acquisition would have on competition in those markets.
"The commission was not satisfied Goodman Fielder would not acquire or strengthen a dominant position in seven markets," Bollard said.
Six of those seven markets related to milling.

The competition concerns that arose in these markets in varying degrees were: high barriers to new entry; a lack of existing or potential competition; suppliers to and acquirers from Goodman would be unable to constrain the company; and the level of market share the combined entity would have (in excess of 80 percent in some markets) if the acquisition went ahead.
Both Goodman Fielder and Defiance Mills are based in Australia and have extensive interests in New Zealand.
Goodman applied to the Commission last month for clearance to acquire the New Zealand baking and milling assets of Defiance.
The agreed purchase price for the assets was NZ$48 million.
New Zealand's Commerce Act prohibits business acquisitions that result in dominance being acquired or strengthened in any markets.
